prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single universal “best” roofer for hail damage — the best contractor for you depends on your ZIP code, roof type, insurance situation, timing, and whether you want manufacturer-certified warranty work. I can find and compare top-rated, hail-experienced roofers near you if you tell me your Denver ZIP code.  

Meanwhile, here’s a quick checklist and tips to help you pick the best hail-damage roofer in Denver:

What to look for
- Hail/insurance experience: ask how many hail claims they handle and if they work with insurance adjusters.  
- Manufacturer certifications: look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, IKO Pro, etc. — these let them offer extended warranties.  
- Local reputation: check recent Google, Yelp, Angi reviews and the BBB for patterns (not just a single 5-star).  
- Proof of insurance and bonding: confirm contractor liability and worker’s comp insurance.  
- Written, itemized estimate: scope of work, materials, disposal, permit fees, timeline.  
- Permits and inspections: reputable roofers pull permits and arrange code inspections.  
- Warranty and workmanship guarantee: get details in writing (length and what it covers).  
- References and photos: ask for recent local hail-damage projects and before/after photos.  
- No high-pressure sales: avoid “storm chasers” who push you to sign immediately or demand full payment up front.  

Practical steps
- Get at least 3 written estimates and compare scope and materials, not only price.  
- Call your insurer to confirm what documentation they want; some adjusters prefer certain documentation.  
- Don’t sign assignment-of-benefits forms without understanding them.  
- If there’s active leaking, get a tarp or emergency repair and a written temporary repair invoice.  

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short list (3–5) of highly rated, hail-experienced Denver roofers in your ZIP and highlight certifications, average review score, and any red flags.  
- Or walk you through questions to ask a roofer on the spot or a template for comparing estimates.

Tell me your ZIP code and whether you’re dealing with an insurance claim, and I’ll find local options.
